title: Taj Mahal Agra - History, Timings, Entry Fee, Travel Tips & Guide
content:
Taj Mahal - Agra,

The Taj Mahal is not just a monument - it is a feeling, a quiet moment in time where love stands still, carved forever in white marble. Built on the banks of the peaceful Yamuna River in Agra, the Taj Mahal is known worldwide as a symbol of eternal love.

Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan built it in memory of his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal, who passed away in 1631. Heartbroken by her death, he decided to create something so beautiful that the world would never forget their love. And truly, time has passed, empires have changed, but the Taj Mahal still stands with the same grace, reminding the world that love has a place in history.

Construction began in 1632 and took almost 22 years, with more than 20,000 craftsmen, artists, and laborers working day and night. The marble used came from Makrana (Rajasthan), precious stones from Persia and Central Asia, and the design represents the best of Persian, Mughal, and Indian architecture.

The first thing most visitors notice is the silence. Even with crowds, there is a calm feeling - the wide gardens, the slow flowing river, the perfect symmetry, and the shining marble that changes color with the light.

  • Morning: soft golden shades
  • Afternoon: bright white and glowing
  • Evening: soft pink tones
  • Full moon night: pearl - like magical shine

Many poets have said the Taj looks like it was carved from moonlight. Standing in front of it, you feel peace. Some people smile, some whisper, and some just sit quietly - everyone responds in their own way.

The Taj Mahal is not only a masterpiece of love but also of design. The four minarets gently lean slightly outward so that if they ever fall, they would fall away from the main tomb. Calligraphy on the walls is so smartly engraved that the letters look equal in size from top to bottom. Inside, Mumtaz and Shah Jahan rest together - as he wished - forever.

Today, the Taj Mahal is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the New 7 Wonders of the World. Millions visit every year, and yet, every visitor walks away with a personal moment - a memory, a whisper, a quiet sigh, a photo, a dream.

If there is one place that every soul should see once in life, it is the Taj Mahal.

Taj Mahal Timings:

  • Sunrise to Sunset,
  • Closed on Fridays (for prayers),

Best viewing times:

  •  Sunrise (most peaceful, most beautiful),
  •  Sunset (warm golden glow),
  •  Full moon night viewing (very limited tickets; magical),
  • 2 - 4 hours, (For deep visit + photography + river view + garden walk),

🎟️ Entry Fees:

  • Indian Citizens - ₹ 50 + ₹ 200 (if visiting mausoleum)
  • SAARC & BIMSTEC Citizens  - ₹ 740
  • Foreign Tourists  -  ₹ 1300 + ₹ 200 (mausoleum optional)
  • Children  - (< 15 years)    Free

Location & Distance from Major Cities:

  • Delhi - 230 km
  • Jaipur - 240 km
  • Lucknow - 335 km
  • Varanasi - 600 km

How to Reach Agra for Taj Mahal explore :

By Air:  Agra Airport (13 km), Delhi Airport (best option for flights, 3 - 4 hrs drive)

By Train: Agra Cantt Railway Station (6 km).

By Road: Yamuna Expressway (from Delhi) - smooth & fast

(Local e-rickshaws, taxis & battery buses available near the entry gate.)

Top Nearby Attractions (within 50 km):

1- Agra Fort -  2 Km from Taj Mahal,

2- Mehtab Bagh (best sunset view) - 1.5 Km from Taj Mahal,

3- Itimad-ud-Daulah (Baby Taj) - 4 Km from Taj Mahal,

4- Akbar’s Tomb, Sikandra - 12 Km from Taj Mahal,

5- Fatehpur Sikri - 40 Km from Taj Mahal,

Things to Do when Taj Mahal Explore:

  • Sunrise photography (best light),
  • Sunset view from Mehtab Bagh,
  • Guided heritage walk,
  • Boat ride on Yamuna (seasonal),
  • Explore Mughal gardens,
  • Try Petha & Mughlai food nearby,
